title: 08. Files & Errors: Requests Module
summary: The requests library is the de facto standard for making HTTP requests in Python. It provides a simple, elegant API for interacting with web services, APIs, and web scraping.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
The `requests` library is the de facto standard for making HTTP requests in Python. It provides a simple, elegant API for interacting with web services, APIs, and web scraping.

**Installation**:

```bash
pip install requests
```

sections.title: Basic Usage
sections.body:
### Making Requests

```python
import requests

# GET request
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/users')

# POST request
response = requests.post('https://api.example.com/users', json={'name': 'Alice'})

# PUT request
response = requests.put('https://api.example.com/users/1', json={'name': 'Bob'})

# DELETE request
response = requests.delete('https://api.example.com/users/1')

# PATCH request
response = requests.patch('https://api.example.com/users/1', json={'age': 30})
```

sections.title: HTTP Methods
sections.body:
| Method  | Purpose                 | Has Body |
| ------- | ----------------------- | -------- |
| GET     | Retrieve data           | No       |
| POST    | Create resource         | Yes      |
| PUT     | Update/replace resource | Yes      |
| PATCH   | Partial update          | Yes      |
| DELETE  | Remove resource         | No       |
| HEAD    | Get headers only        | No       |
| OPTIONS | Get supported methods   | No       |

sections.title: Response Object
sections.body:
```python
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data')

# Status code
print(response.status_code)  # 200

# Response body (text)
print(response.text)

# Response body (JSON)
data = response.json()

# Response headers
print(response.headers)

# Response encoding
print(response.encoding)

# Raw bytes
print(response.content)

# Check if successful
if response.ok:  # True if status_code < 400
    print("Success!")

# Raise exception for error status
response.raise_for_status()
```

sections.title: Status Codes
sections.body:
| Range | Category      | Examples                                         |
| ----- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| 1xx   | Informational | 100 Continue                                     |
| 2xx   | Success       | 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content              |
| 3xx   | Redirection   | 301 Moved, 302 Found, 304 Not Modified           |
| 4xx   | Client Error  | 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found |
| 5xx   | Server Error  | 500 Internal Error, 503 Service Unavailable      |

sections.title: Request Parameters
sections.body:
### Query Parameters

```python
# Using params parameter
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/search',
                       params={'q': 'python', 'page': 1})
# URL: https://api.example.com/search?q=python&page=1

# Multiple values for same key
params = {'id': ['1', '2', '3']}
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/items', params=params)
```

### Request Body

```python
# JSON body
response = requests.post('https://api.example.com/users',
                        json={'name': 'Alice', 'age': 30})

# Form data
response = requests.post('https://api.example.com/login',
                        data={'username': 'alice', 'password': 'secret'})

# Raw body
response = requests.post('https://api.example.com/data',
                        data='raw string data',
                        headers={'Content-Type': 'text/plain'})
```

sections.title: Headers
sections.body:
```python
# Custom headers
headers = {
    'User-Agent': 'MyApp/1.0',
    'Accept': 'application/json',
    'Authorization': 'Bearer token123'
}

response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data', headers=headers)

# View response headers
print(response.headers['Content-Type'])
print(response.headers.get('X-Custom-Header', 'default'))
```

sections.title: Authentication
sections.body:
### Basic Authentication

```python
from requests.auth import HTTPBasicAuth

response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data',
                       auth=HTTPBasicAuth('username', 'password'))

# Shorthand
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data',
                       auth=('username', 'password'))
```

### Bearer Token

```python
headers = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}'}
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data', headers=headers)
```

### API Key

```python
# In headers
headers = {'X-API-Key': 'your-api-key'}
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data', headers=headers)

# In query parameters
params = {'api_key': 'your-api-key'}
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data', params=params)
```

sections.title: Sessions
sections.body:
Sessions allow you to persist parameters across requests.

```python
session = requests.Session()

# Set default headers
session.headers.update({'User-Agent': 'MyApp/1.0'})

# Set default authentication
session.auth = ('username', 'password')

# Make requests
response1 = session.get('https://api.example.com/users')
response2 = session.get('https://api.example.com/posts')

# Session maintains cookies
session.close()  # Always close when done
```

### Context Manager

```python
with requests.Session() as session:
    session.headers.update({'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}'})
    response = session.get('https://api.example.com/data')
# Session automatically closed
```

sections.title: Timeouts
sections.body:
```python
# Timeout in seconds
try:
    response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data', timeout=5)
except requests.Timeout:
    print("Request timed out")

# Separate connect and read timeouts
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data', timeout=(3, 10))
# (connect_timeout, read_timeout)
```

sections.title: Error Handling
Retries
sections.body:
```python
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from requests.packages.urllib3.util.retry import Retry

session = requests.Session()

# Configure retry strategy
retry_strategy = Retry(
    total=3,  # Total retries
    status_forcelist=[429, 500, 502, 503, 504],  # Status codes to retry
    backoff_factor=1  # Wait 1, 2, 4 seconds between retries
)

adapter = HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retry_strategy)
session.mount("http://", adapter)
session.mount("https://", adapter)

response = session.get('https://api.example.com/data')
```

sections.title: File Upload
sections.body:
```python
# Upload single file
files = {'file': open('report.pdf', 'rb')}
response = requests.post('https://api.example.com/upload', files=files)

# Upload with additional data
files = {'file': open('report.pdf', 'rb')}
data = {'description': 'Monthly report'}
response = requests.post('https://api.example.com/upload',
                        files=files, data=data)

# Multiple files
files = [
    ('file', open('file1.txt', 'rb')),
    ('file', open('file2.txt', 'rb'))
]
response = requests.post('https://api.example.com/upload', files=files)
```

sections.title: File Download
sections.body:
```python
# Download to memory
response = requests.get('https://example.com/file.pdf')
with open('file.pdf', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(response.content)

# Stream large files
response = requests.get('https://example.com/large-file.zip', stream=True)
with open('large-file.zip', 'wb') as f:
    for chunk in response.iter_content(chunk_size=8192):
        f.write(chunk)
```

sections.title: Cookies
sections.body:
```python
# Send cookies
cookies = {'session_id': 'abc123'}
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data', cookies=cookies)

# Access response cookies
print(response.cookies)
print(response.cookies['session_id'])

# Session cookies
session = requests.Session()
response = session.get('https://example.com/login')
# Cookies automatically maintained in session
```

sections.title: Proxies
sections.body:
```python
proxies = {
    'http': 'http://10.10.1.10:3128',
    'https': 'http://10.10.1.10:1080',
}

response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data', proxies=proxies)
```

sections.title: SSL Verification
sections.body:
```python
# Disable SSL verification (not recommended for production)
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data', verify=False)

# Custom CA bundle
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data', verify='/path/to/ca_bundle.crt')
```

sections.title: Streaming Responses
sections.body:
```python
# Stream large responses
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/stream', stream=True)

for line in response.iter_lines():
    if line:
        print(line.decode('utf-8'))
```

sections.title: Best Practices
sections.body:
1. **Always use timeouts**: Prevent hanging requests
2. **Handle exceptions**: Use try/except for robust error handling
3. **Use sessions for multiple requests**: Improves performance
4. **Close sessions**: Always close or use context managers
5. **Validate SSL certificates**: Don't disable in production
6. **Use appropriate HTTP methods**: Follow REST conventions
7. **Set User-Agent**: Identify your application
8. **Implement retries**: Handle transient failures
9. **Stream large files**: Don't load everything into memory
10. **Rate limiting**: Respect API rate limits

sections.title: Common Patterns
Performance Tips
sections.body:
1. **Use Session**: Reuses TCP connections (connection pooling)
2. **Stream large responses**: Use `stream=True` for large files
3. **Compress requests**: Enable gzip compression
4. **Connection pooling**: Sessions automatically handle this
5. **Async requests**: Consider `httpx` for async support

sections.title: Alternative Libraries
sections.body:
- **httpx**: Modern async-capable alternative to requests
- **aiohttp**: Async HTTP client/server
- **urllib3**: Lower-level HTTP library (requests uses this)
- **httplib2**: Another HTTP library (less popular)

sections.title: Common Use Cases
sections.body:
1. **REST API consumption**: Most common use case
2. **Web scraping**: Fetch HTML pages
3. **File download/upload**: Transfer files over HTTP
4. **Webhooks**: Send notifications
5. **Testing APIs**: Automated API testing
6. **Data collection**: Gather data from web services
7. **Microservice communication**: Service-to-service calls
8. **OAuth flows**: Authentication workflows
